cases.result_scope: symptom score at week 12 in all randomized participants

passages.text: The trial was open label and participants and treating clinicians knew the assigned intervention.
One participant independently stopped study tablets because of nausea; outcome follow-up continued and trial staff did not direct a treatment change.
The protocol permits temporary interruption or discontinuation for toxicity while outcome follow-up continues.

premises.rationale: The conduct passage distinguishes an ordinary participant choice from a change caused by trial personnel or trial procedures.
The pair establishes the observed interruption and that toxicity interruption was protocol permitted.

cases.result_scope: symptom score at week 12 in all randomized participants

passages.text: The trial was open label and participants and treating clinicians knew the assigned intervention.
Because clinicians expected toxicity, trial staff scheduled extra monitoring only in the experimental group and directed twelve participants to switch to a prohibited therapy before week 12.
The prohibited switch occurred in twelve experimental-group participants and no control-group participants, before measurement of the week 12 symptom score.

premises.rationale: The passage explicitly links the protocol-inconsistent switch to assignment-aware trial staff and trial-specific monitoring.
The passages locate the differential change before the approved outcome time point and report its arm imbalance.

cases.result_scope: relapse by day 90 in all randomized participants

passages.text: Twelve participants discontinued assigned treatment before day 90.
Relapse status at day 90 was obtained for all 200 randomized participants, including all twelve who discontinued treatment.
Administrative censoring begins after the prespecified day 90 endpoint and does not remove day 90 relapse observations.

premises.rationale: Treatment discontinuation is not missing outcome data when the approved outcome remains observed.
Administrative censoring after the compatible endpoint does not imply missing day 90 outcome data.

cases.result_scope: relapse by day 90 in all randomized participants

passages.text: Twelve participants discontinued assigned treatment before day 90.
The twelve participants who discontinued because their symptoms worsened were lost to follow-up and had no recorded relapse status at day 90.
Day 90 relapse status was observed for 188 of 200 randomized participants; all twelve unavailable outcomes were in participants who withdrew after symptom worsening.

premises.rationale: Either passage establishes that the approved day 90 outcome is actually unavailable, not merely that treatment stopped.
The withdrawal reason links missingness to worsening symptoms and therefore to the possible true outcome value.

cases.result_scope: relapse by day 90 in all randomized participants using a risk ratio

passages.text: A statistical analysis plan was prepared before analysis.
Version 1.0, signed before database unblinding, specifies relapse by day 90, all randomized participants, risk ratio estimation, and multiple imputation as the missing-data method.
The reported result is the day 90 relapse risk ratio in all randomized participants using the prespecified multiple-imputation analysis.

premises.rationale: The exact analysis detail and finalization before unblinded outcome access are both stated.
The plan and report match on endpoint, time point, population, estimator, and missing-data method.

cases.result_scope: relapse by day 90 in all randomized participants using a risk ratio

passages.text: A statistical analysis plan was prepared before analysis.
The undated plan states only that outcomes will be compared between groups and does not identify the time point, population, estimator, or missing-data method.
The report presents several relapse time points and adjusted and unadjusted estimates without stating which analysis was selected before unblinded outcome data were available.

premises.rationale: Plan existence alone does not establish exact detail or finalization before unblinded outcome access.
The available plan cannot be matched to the reported population, time point, estimator, or missing-data method.
